D.t: Peggy Flanagan leads by 12.4 in the forecast and wins 98% of simulations. The cushion is about 346,607 votes; a one point swing is about 13,999 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +5.6 and D +19.2. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +8.4. Your best recent poll is New York Times/Siena at D +13.3; your worst is InsiderAdvantage at D +1.1. 11 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Hennepin, a projected net 340,093 votes; Ramsey, a projected net 139,797 votes; Dakota, a projected net 42,052 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Anoka, D +2.5, 6.3% of the vote; Scott, R +6.0, 2.7% of the vote; Carver, R +4.6, 2.1% of the vote; Rice, D +3.9, 1.1% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Peggy Flanagan runs furthest behind in Carver, Crow Wing, Wright. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 87% of voters, 52 to 46, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.36 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 75% of voters, 55 to 43, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.75 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 58% of voters, 59 to 39, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.90 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Peggy Flanagan: Immigration voters 27 to 71, Small counties 37 to 61, Incomes $125K and up 46 to 52. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$1.1M cash against $1.4M. Roughly even money; the air war will be decided by outside groups and earned media.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.1 points away from Peggy Flanagan. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
Activity: 3 campaign stops by the candidate or surrogates in 30 days.

R.t: Michele Tafoya trails by 12.4 and wins 2% of simulations. Closing it takes about 173,304 voters switching sides, or 346,607 more net votes from new turnout.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Wright, a projected net 20,078 votes; Stearns, a projected net 16,810 votes; Sherburne, a projected net 15,693 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Anoka, D +2.5, 6.3% of the vote; Scott, R +6.0, 2.7% of the vote; Carver, R +4.6, 2.1% of the vote; Rice, D +3.9, 1.1% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Michele Tafoya runs furthest behind in St. Louis, Ramsey, Olmsted. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 87% of voters, 46 to 52, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.36 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 75% of voters, 43 to 55, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.75 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 58% of voters, 39 to 59, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.90 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Michele Tafoya: Black voters 15 to 82, Asian and other voters 23 to 74, Corruption voters 24 to 73. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$1.4M cash against $1.1M. Roughly even money; the air war will be decided by outside groups and earned media.
